            Backup time: any time. 0 restore points or 0 days means no limit.
          

          
          

            ⚠ Include credentials stores this router’s passwords and keys on this server, encrypted at rest.
          

          

            A backup is stored only when the configuration actually changed, so a
            frequent schedule costs a short check rather than disk. Each restore point
            is a pair: an export for the diff, and an encrypted binary for the restore.

              signs in with; no other profile can take its account or its group.

            Notification channels
            

              
            

          

          

            
Configure notification channels to receive alerts about your
              routers. Supports SMTP email and webhook URLs (Telegram, Discord, Slack, ntfy, Gotify,
              Pushover, Pushbullet, and anything else through an Apprise server).

            
            
MikroDash records every alert. Each channel chooses which of them
              it delivers, and which routers it covers.

Off means no login at all: anyone who can reach this page can see every router. Changing router configuration needs sign-in, so write pages are read-only while this is off. Only sensible on a trusted network.

            AI Agent
          

          

            

              Connects to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint: a hosted provider, a gateway, or a
              model running on your own hardware. A hosted endpoint sends router
              names, addresses and network shape to that provider. A local one
              (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, LiteLLM) sends nothing outside your network.
              The AI Agent page appears once this is switched on and an endpoint and model are set.
            

            
            

              

                
                
                

              

              

                
                
                

              

              

                
                
                

              

              

                
                
                

              

              

                
                
                

              

              

                
                
                
The most the model may write in one reply, its reasoning included. A reasoning model that runs out writes nothing; raise it if answers come back cut off.

              

              

                
                
                

              

              

                
                
                
For an endpoint on your own network with a self-signed certificate. Press
                  Test Connection: if the certificate is not trusted, it is shown with a
                  Trust button that fills this in, then save. Only that exact certificate is
                  accepted afterwards.

              

            

            
            

              
              
            

            

            
            

              

                
                
                
The assistant can only change things you are allowed to change yourself, and
                  every change goes through the same checks, confirmation and audit trail as the
                  forms. Turning this off lets it apply ordinary changes without
                  asking. A change that could cut MikroDash off from the router is always
                  put to you, whatever this is set to.

              

              

                
                
                
For what no page covers. Offered only to signed-in global administrators, and
                  every command, even a read, is shown to you and runs only when you type the
                  router's name. Raw commands skip MikroDash's own checks, read-back and
                  undo, so leave this off unless you need it.

              

            

          

        


        
        

          

            
            System Prompt
            
          

          

            

              Who the assistant is and how it behaves. Edit it to change its tone, to tell it
              about your network, or to give it standing instructions.
              MikroDash’s own safety rules are always applied on top of this and
              cannot be edited here, so the assistant still refuses to follow
              instructions found in router data, and still cannot run commands or reach any
              device other than the one selected.
            

            

              

                
                
                
0 / 8000Leave it empty to use the built-in prompt.

              

            

            
            
            
            

              

                
                
                
Writes a one-line router status on the Dashboard.

              

              

                
                

                  
                  h
                  
                  s
                

                
Between 1 minute and 24 hours. 0 hours gives the interval in seconds only.

              

            

            

              Off by default. The card asks the model only while it is on your Dashboard and
              the Dashboard is open, and by default at most once every 3 hours (10800
              seconds); coming back sooner shows the last line again rather than asking. On a
              hosted endpoint every refresh is billable, including the refresh icon on the card.
            

            

              

                
                
                
The card’s terminal text. MikroDash blue by default.

              

              

                
                
                
0 / 500What the card is asked to write. Leave it empty to use the built-in prompt;

            Zero-touch provisioning
          

          

            

              New routers run a short script and call home to this MikroDash, then join the fleet on
              their own. A remote router dials in over a WireGuard tunnel built into MikroDash, so it
              can sit behind NAT anywhere. This opens one UDP port, which must be
              published from the container and reachable from the internet; it stays closed while this
              is off. Routers on your own network need no tunnel.
            

            

            
            

              

                
                
                

              

              

                
                
                
A name or IP, with no port.

              

              

                
                
                

              

              

                
                
                
Private, and not used on your routers' networks.

              

              

                
                
                
Where local routers call home. The wizard suggests it.

              

            

            

              
Instance
-

              
Public key
-

            

            
Every script carries this instance's key, so a router can only ever call
              home to this MikroDash.

          

        

        

          

            Generic scripts
          

          

            

              One script for many routers, for a rollout. Each router that runs it appears on the Devices
              page as Not yet provisioned, and joins the fleet when you onboard it. It
              needs provisioning switched on and the address above.

            DNS tools
          

          

            
Each is off until you switch it on, and off it draws nothing and reads nothing.

            

              

                
                
                
Tick static entries on the DNS page to change their address list, forwarder or state, or remove them, in one job paced by the write limit; export the table as a RouterOS script or CSV.

              

              

                
                
                
Administrators: a Cache card on the DNS page that reads the resolver's cache when you press Read, searchable. The cache lists every name the network has looked up, so DNS read access alone does not open it. Nothing is read in the background.

              

              

                
                
                
Why a domain does or does not take its route: the static entry that catches it, what it resolved to, whether the address reached the list, and the mangle rule and route behind it.

              

              

                
                
                
In the fleet comparison, make the other routers' static entries match one router: add and change, and remove only if you choose to, after the counts are shown. Dynamic entries are never touched.

              

              

                
                
                
Administrators: keep FWD entries in step with a list of domains, pasted or fetched from a public URL, on the routers you pick. Only entries the list created are changed, and a fetch that comes back empty or under half its last size changes nothing on its own.

              

            

          

        

        

          

            
            Monitoring and Wi-Fi
          

          

            

              

                
                
                
A Dashboard card for the address list your FWD entries feed: its size, the mangle rules that use it and the route they mark for, with an alert when that route stays down for three minutes. Only routers whose static entries feed the list are read, a few filtered prints a minute.

              

              

                
                
                
The list the card and the alert are about. Nothing is read until it is named.

              

              

                
                
                
Alert when a device you mark as watched is gone from Wi-Fi and from the router's ARP table for longer than its grace time. Those two are read on a router only while a device on it is watched.

              

              

                
                
                
Record each Wi-Fi client's signal and access point once a minute, so a client's name on Wifi Clients opens its history. Recording is switched on per router, on that page; only those routers have their Wi-Fi clients read while nobody has them open.

              

              

                
                
                

              

              

                
                
                
Colour each access point on the Wi-Fi map by its clients' average signal and list the clients below -75 dBm. Reads nothing new.

              

              

                
                
                
Compare every CAP's RouterOS version with the manager's on the CAPsMAN page, and upgrade the ones behind from the manager.

      New credential profile
    

    

      
      

        

          
          
          

        

        

          
          
          
The account created on every linked router.
            It cannot be the account MikroDash signs in with.

        

        

          
          
          

        

        

          
          
          
Required for a new profile. Leave blank when
            editing to keep the current password.

        

        

          
          
          
A starting point. Every permission is
            yours to change, and the profile gets a RouterOS group of its own holding exactly what you tick - it
            never joins one of the router's existing groups.

        

      

      

        

          
          
          
Created on each linked router, and used by this profile
            alone. It cannot be renamed later: that would be a migration across every linked device, not an edit.

        

        

          
          
          
Offered first when a device is provisioned. Only one profile can be the
            default, so turning this on clears it from whichever profile holds it now.

        

        

          
          

          

        

      

      

    

    

      
      
    

   

  


  
  

   

    

      Where this profile applies
    

    

      
Pick routers, or a site: every router in a picked site gets
        the account, now and as the site changes, and one that leaves the site has it taken off. Nothing changes
        until Apply.

      

      

    

    

      
      
      
    

   

  


  
  
  

   

    

      Import devices
    

    

      

        
One device per row. Only host is
          required, plus a login: a username and password, or a credential profile. A profile with no password
          signs in with the profile's account, which must already exist on the router; that is not checked
          during the import, so a wrong one shows on the Devices page as a sign-in error. A profile with the
          router's username and password adds it on that login, then creates the account in the background
          (Credential Profiles shows how it went). Several sites go in one cell separated by
          |, and missing ones are created. Devices already in MikroDash are skipped.

        

          
          
        

      

      

      

      

    

    

      
      
    

   

  


  

   

    

      MikroDash login
    

    

      
AccountmikrodashGroupmikrodash

      

        

          
          
          

        

        

          
          
          

        

      

      
At least 12 characters. It signs in to every linked device with
        every permission, so treat it like the devices' admin password.

      

    

    

      
      
    

   

  


  
  

   

    

      Devices
    

    

      
Linking creates user mikrodash in group mikrodash on the
        device, signs in with it to prove it works, and only then switches MikroDash over. If it does not work the
        device is put back as it was. Picking a site adds the devices in it now; one that joins it later is not
        added.

      

      

    

    

      
      
    

   

  


  
  

   

    

      Use its own login
    

    

      
This device will sign in with the
        account below instead of the profile. The MikroDash account stays on the router.

      

        

          
          
          

        

        

          
          
          

        

      

      

    

    

      
      
    

   

  


  

   

    

      Switch to API-SSL
    

    

      

        On this device this creates a certificate authority and a
        server certificate, then enables API-SSL on port 8729 and moves MikroDash onto it.
      

      

        Generating two keys can take a minute or two on small hardware. The plain API is left
        enabled as a way back in, and MikroDash moves only after the device answers on 8729.
